sourceBindings.text: A coloured solution is not a pH result until you know which sample, kit, reagent and chart produced it. In this step you practise the full sequence on one documented field kit, then learn how to transfer the method to the actual kit in a trainer-supervised laboratory.

Under trainer observation, identify the actual kit and its manual, measure sample, reagent and water to its markings, close and mix as specified, and wait for the required settling and colour-development condition.

Compare the clear liquid only with the colour chart supplied for the same pH comparator under suitable light, record the closest supported pH or chart interval and uncertainty, and preserve sample and kit identity.

Select task-appropriate PPE and the reagent's SDS, clean equipment and dispose of waste per site rule, and explain when a field colour kit is enough and when calibrated digital/laboratory measurement is needed.

sourceBindings.text: A student holds a violet pH solution beside a chart borrowed from an unrelated NPK kit.
Stop: the chart may use a different indicator and colour response, so the appearance is not a valid pH reading.
Find the chart supplied with the exact pH comparator and compare its liquid in suitable light.
If no matching chart or manual exists, mark unassessed and use a documented kit or laboratory.
A colour has meaning only inside its own method.

sourceBindings.text: A soybean crop is stunted and yellow, and the grower asks whether soil pH is the problem.
Inspect where symptoms occur and check roots, moisture and field pattern; collect a representative sample using the relevant crop protocol.
Use a matched colour kit or calibrated digital meter for initial pH, and send an appropriate sample for laboratory confirmation and nutrient/soil interpretation if management is contemplated.

If the soil is sufficiently acidic, liming might be considered; if high-pH, a crop/soil-specific acidification or other management strategy might be considered. A product, dose and timing require local test guidance; yellowing alone proves neither case.
Measure and diagnose first; recommend a crop-specific adjustment only with supporting evidence.

sourceBindings.text: Choose a labelled sample and the Rapitest 1601 pH comparator, then place the eight actions in order: check label/SDS and chart; add soil to its line; add the matching pH capsule; add water to its line; cap/shake; wait for settling/colour; compare above-soil liquid with its chart in diffuse daylight; record result and clean by site procedure. Reject an NPK chart, arbitrary reagent amount or invented precise reading.

Trainer selects the actual kit, verifies manual/SDS and pretests samples A/B/C. Each learner measures under observation, records actual result and uncertainty, cleans and disposes safely. Group recorder/analyst roles rotate, but one learner's test does not pass another.

Method
Useful strength
Limit and next check

sourceBindings.text: colorimetric
A method that compares a developed colour with a method-specific reference chart.
comparator
The kit's chamber and matched colour chart used to judge a test result.
reagent
A test chemical used according to its own label, SDS and manufacturer procedure.
resolution
The smallest pH difference supported by a chart or device; do not invent finer readings.
calibration
Checking and adjusting a digital meter against known buffer standards according to its method.
